name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,353

clue.text: Restraint limiting attempt to turn at the same time

indicators.note: to turn something round is to face it the other way, so this word is read backwards
limiting means hemming in, so one word sits inside the other as a boundary

blocks.note: a tether is a rope that restrains an animal
to have a go is to make an attempt

explanation.surface: A tethered animal is held back from turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things together means doing them simultaneously, a plain adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Fool performer with good write-up

indicators.note: in a down clue, written up means written from the bottom upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a turn is a variety act or its performer
pi is short for pious, so good

explanation.surface: A comic actor earns a glowing review.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnip is British slang for a dim-witted person, the vegetable used as an insult.

clue.text: Country doctor introduced to Phoebe's mum

indicators.note: introduced to means placed inside, so one piece is inserted into the other

blocks.note: in Greek myth the Titan Phoebe was a daughter of Gaia, the Earth
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: A country GP is introduced to a friend's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country doctor' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'Country' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gambia is a small West African nation surrounded by Senegal, a specific example.

clue.text: Retire from shop

blocks.note: first meaning: to go to bed for the night
second meaning: to inform on or betray someone to the police

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shop' looks like a store but is British slang for informing on someone to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both going to bed at night and handing a wrongdoer over to the authorities.

clue.text: United supporter overcome by result in the end

blocks.note: an event can mean an outcome
U is the abbreviation for United in team names
an ally supports you

explanation.surface: A United fan is overwhelmed by the final score.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'overcome by' means placed beneath, so the result goes on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventually means finally or after some time, an adverbial synonym for the phrase.

clue.text: What Robert Catesby became after going around Spain regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter of the word is kept
going around means encircling, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: past means after, as in half past ten
the second and fourth letters of the country's name

explanation.surface: A historical note on the Gunpowder Plotter's travels in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Catesby led the 1605 Gunpowder Plot and was a Catholic who had returned to the faith; papist is an old hostile word for a Roman Catholic.
explanation.definitionFit: Catesby converted to Roman Catholicism, and papist was the derogatory term for followers of the Pope.

clue.text: Fair enough!

blocks.note: first meaning: reasonable, middling, passable
second meaning: sufficient for the purpose

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'Fair enough!' reads as a single shrug of agreement; split, each word is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both passably good and sufficient in quantity for a need.

clue.text: Ridiculous claim to hold up popular setter as unfriendly

indicators.note: something ridiculous is absurd and out of order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
the setter refers to themselves as I
taken as written

explanation.surface: An absurd accusation is made to discredit a well-liked puzzle compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, to hold up is to support from below, so the shuffled word sits under the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Inimical means hostile or harmful, from the Latin for enemy, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Lie around the whole time? It's unbelievable

definitions.note: a phrase describing the answer: a story that cannot be believed

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: a tale can be a lie
all means the whole
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone who lies all the time can't be believed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tale is an exaggerated story too far-fetched to credit, an idiom.

clue.text: Observed fellow cutting grass

indicators.note: cutting into something means slicing into its middle, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a reed is a tall marsh grass
Mark is a man's name, so a fellow

explanation.surface: Someone noticed a man slicing through the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe can mean to comment, as in 'he observed that it was late', which is to say something aloud as a passing remark.

clue.text: Servant returning home tucks into something to eat

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read from right to left
tucks into means is placed snugly inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: being in is being at home
a meal is food eaten at one sitting

explanation.surface: A domestic servant comes home and tucks into a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a menial is a domestic worker doing lowly household tasks.

clue.text: Start to get involved with Italian volunteers sent back to occupy the centre of Chieti

indicators.note: sent back means returned the way they came, so the letters run right to left
the centre of a word is its middle, so only the two central letters are kept
to occupy a place is to sit within it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to be in on something is to be involved
It is the abbreviation for Italian, as in It vermouth
the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
the third and fourth of its six letters

explanation.surface: Instructions for joining an Italian volunteer force and taking over a town.
explanation.walkthrough: Chieti is a town in central Italy, chosen to suit the Italian surface. The volunteers are the TA, the Territorial Army.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate something is to begin it or set it going, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: One barely seen by short head girl on street

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: nut is slang for the head
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A head girl spotted on the street, seemingly at a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes naked is seen bare, the playful sense of barely here, so this defines a naturist.

clue.text: The determination of a dispute with Hamlet for instance

blocks.note: first meaning: the resolving of a quarrel by agreement
second meaning: a small village, a place where people have settled

explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet looks like Shakespeare's prince, whose famous indecision makes 'determination' seem ironic, but here a hamlet is a tiny village.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both an agreement ending a legal quarrel and a community of houses such as a village.

clue.text: The first to complain after priest hides copy of evidence of activity

indicators.note: something that hides another keeps it concealed inside, so one word wraps the other
the first of a word means its opening letter only

blocks.note: Pr is the abbreviation for priest
to ape is to imitate or copy
the opening letter of the little word
to rail is to complain bitterly

explanation.surface: Someone complains after a priest conceals a copy of something incriminating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The first to' looks like a person, the first one to complain, but it is just the first letter of 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper trail is the documents left behind that record what somebody has done, an idiom.

clue.text: Get used to Bill meeting a client without hesitation

indicators.note: without means lacking, and a hesitation is the sound er, so that sound is removed

blocks.note: ac is the abbreviation for account, a bill
a customer is a client

explanation.surface: A shop greets a customer and hands over the bill without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: Er is the hesitation sound, so it is the part dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To accustom someone is to make them familiar with something, so the phrase is a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Several transferred after QPR's latest defeat

indicators.note: transferred means moved about, so these letters are relocated into a new order
the latest is the most recent, so the last letter of the name is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of the club's initials
taken as written

explanation.surface: Several players leave the football club after its latest loss.
explanation.walkthrough: QPR is Queens Park Rangers, a London football club, and transferred hints at players moving clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal can mean a setback or defeat, a change of fortune for the worse.

clue.text: Working in addition to supporting Democrat whenever required

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece holds the other up from below, so the joining word is written after the party abbreviation

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
Dem is short for Democrat
and adds one thing to another

explanation.surface: An aide works extra hours to back a Democrat politician whenever called.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' means sitting underneath, so the joining word goes below the party abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: On demand means available as soon as asked for, an idiom for whenever someone needs it.

clue.text: Catholic film director's departed to make a fresh start

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Catholic
David Lean, director of Lawrence of Arabia, with the 's
the late someone is a person who has died

explanation.surface: A dead Catholic film-maker's legacy is wiped away for a new beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean slate is an idiom for a record wiped clear so one can begin again.

clue.text: Employ a couple of Ethiopians during bad weather

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a couple means two, so the opening pair of letters of the word
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: Hiring two Ethiopian workers in a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: To retain someone, such as a lawyer, is to engage their services for a fee.

clue.text: Film's iconic opening set in an Indian city

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so only the first letter of the word is kept
set in means placed inside, so one piece is inserted into the other

blocks.note: Patna is the capital of Bihar state
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A classic film's famous opening scene is set in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie, as the surface insists, but it is a thin coating.
explanation.definitionFit: A patina is a thin surface layer, like the green coating on old bronze.

clue.text: Be obliged to admit fellow sent north is on the tail of Red Guard

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside the other
in a down clue, going north means travelling upwards, so the letters read backwards
the tail of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: if you need to do something you are obliged to
F is the abbreviation for fellow
the final letter of the colour

explanation.surface: A fellow is forced to pursue the Red Guard, Mao's young militia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Guard' looks like one name, the Chinese militia, but the definition is 'Guard' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To guard and to defend both mean to protect someone or something from attack.

clue.text: Inconsistent comedian at last packing questionable venue

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word only
something questionable is doubtful or not right, so these letters are not in their proper order
packing means stuffed inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comic plays erratically at a dubious club.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneven performance varies in quality, so it is irregular and lacks consistency.

clue.text: Produce information on deserter found in the middle of Leek

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside, so one piece is placed within the other
the middle of a word is its central part, here the two central letters

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
the two central letters of the four
a rat deserts a sinking ship

explanation.surface: Reporting on an army deserter tracked down in the Staffordshire town of Leek.
explanation.walkthrough: Leek is a market town in Staffordshire, England; capitalised to hide the letters it lends.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate is to bring into being or create, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Remained unused on the way back with fellow Dutch navigator

indicators.note: on the way back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word reads right to left

blocks.note: something that sat on a shelf remained idle
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A sailor stays idle on the return voyage with a Dutch companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Abel Tasman was the 17th-century explorer who reached Tasmania and New Zealand, a specific example.

clue.text: Reject determined to join top class team

blocks.note: set on something means determined
A is the top grade
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A player rejected but resolved to join an elite team.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something aside is to put it out of consideration, dismissing or overruling it, as with a verdict.

clue.text: Furious about fellow coming back and ready finally to make a complaint

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so the name is read from right to left
about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other
finally points to the last letter of the word only

blocks.note: mad means very angry
Al is a man's name
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An angry man comes back, ready to lodge a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' looks like a grumble, but here it is the medical sense of an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in medical usage is an ailment or disorder, as is a malady.

clue.text: Touchstone finds a way after resistance by Audrey at first

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the name only

blocks.note: to make a stand is to resist
the opening letter of the name
Rd is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Touchstone, the clown in As You Like It, finds his way to Audrey, the goatherd he woos.
explanation.walkthrough: Touchstone and Audrey are lovers in Shakespeare's As You Like It, so the names seem to be characters, not a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchstone was a stone for testing gold, hence any benchmark or criterion for judging quality.
